question: A 27-year-old woman goes to the genetic counseling clinic after having a child with Down syndrome. In the child, a trisomy 21 with translocation 21/21 inherited from the mother is identified. What would be the risk of recurrence of Down syndrome in the future children of this woman?

options.opa: The risk of recurrence will be 10-15%, as in the rest of translocations.
options.opb: 100% of viable fetuses will be born with Down syndrome.
options.opc: The risk of recurrence will be very low (12%).
options.opd: The risk of recurrence will be 50%.

enhanced_information: In the case of a 21/21 translocation in the mother, all her gametes will carry an extra chromosome 21. This is because the translocation results in gametes that either have two chromosome 21s or none, but viable offspring can only result from gametes with two chromosome 21s. Therefore, all viable offspring will inherit an extra chromosome 21, leading to Down syndrome. The risk of recurrence for Down syndrome in future children of this woman is 100% for viable pregnancies. The retrieved evidence path, while broad, supports the understanding that germ cells with genetic alterations can lead to conditions like trisomy, aligning with the consensus that a 21/21 translocation results in all viable offspring having Down syndrome.
